newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon says peace process at critical stage.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon says peace process at critical stage.

text.p: Lebanese President Elias Hrawi said on Tuesday the Arab-Israeli peace process was at a critical stage and that the only solution for peace with the Jewish state would be a complete Israeli withdrawal from south Lebanon.
"The peace process has entered the crossroad of decision," Hrawi said in a speech at a banquet he hosted for the holy Moslem month of Ramadan.

"We say that the problem is not whether the talks (between Lebanon and Israel) resume or not and we say that the solution is that Israel implement (U.N.) Resolution 425 and that we gain back our full sovereignty," he added.
Security Council Resolution 425, which was issued in 1978, calls for a complete and unconditional Israeli troops withdrawal from south Lebanon where Israel occupies a border zone.

Peace talks between Lebanon and Israel are stalled over the issue of an Israeli pullout from the 15-km (nine-miles)-deep zone it set up to protect its northern border area against cross-frontier attacks.

"The yardstick of just and comprehensive peace is returning the land, all the land up to the last grain of sand on the internationally recognised border, in line with the Madrid conference resolutions," Hrawi said.

The Madrid peace conference of 1991, which drew Arab and Israeli delegates to the negotiating table, set the formula of exchanging occupied Arab land for peace with the Jewish state as the basis for the peace negotiations.
Lebanon and Syria use a hand-in-hand approach in their negotiations with Israel. Syria is Lebanon's main power broker with 35,000 troops stationed there.
